The '''2000–01 Primeira Liga''' was the [[Primeira Liga#All-time Primeira Liga table|67th edition]] of the top flight of Portuguese football. It started on 19 August 2000 with a match between [[S.C. Braga|Braga]] and [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]], and ended on 27 May 2001. The league was contested by 18 clubs, with [[Sporting CP]] as the defending champions.

[[Boavista F.C.|Boavista]] won their first league title, becoming only the second champions from outside the [[Big Three (Portugal)|Portuguese "Big Three" (''Os Três Grandes'')]] of [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], [[FC Porto|Porto]] and Sporting, after [[C.F. Os Belenenses|Belenenses]] in the [[1945–46 Primeira Divisão|1945–46 season]]. Boavista qualified for the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League group stage]] along with Porto, who entered the second qualifying round. Sporting and [[C.S. Marítimo|Marítimo]] qualified for the [[2001–02 UEFA Cup]]. At the bottom of the table, [[S.C. Campomaiorense|Campomaiorense]], [[C.D. Aves|Desportivo das Aves]] and [[C.F. Estrela da Amadora|Estrela da Amadora]] were relegated to the [[Segunda Liga]]. [[Pena (footballer)|Pena]] finished as the top scorer with 22 goals. This season saw also [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] finish sixth, their lowest ever Primeira Liga position.

==Promotion and relegation==

===Teams relegated to [[Segunda Liga]]===
*[[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]]
*[[Rio Ave F.C.|Rio Ave]]
*[[C.D. Santa Clara|Santa Clara]]

Vitória de Setúbal, Rio Ave and Santa Clara were consigned to the Segunda Liga after finishing as the bottom three teams in [[1999–2000 Primeira Liga|1999–2000 season]].

===Teams promoted from Segunda Liga===
*[[F.C. Paços de Ferreira|Paços de Ferreira]]
*[[S.C. Beira-Mar|Beira-Mar]]
*[[C.D. Aves|Desportivo das Aves]]

The other three teams were replaced by Paços de Ferreira, Beira-Mar and Desportivo das Aves from the Segunda Liga.
